ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$, $\angle BAC=70^\circ$, $\odot O$ is the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$, point D is on the minor arc $\overset{\frown}{AC}$. What is the degree measure of $\angle D$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given that AB=AC, and $\angle$BAC=$70^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle$B=$\angle$ACB=$55^\circ$, \\
since quadrilateral ABCD is inscribed in circle O, \\
therefore $\angle$D=$180^\circ$−$\angle$B=$\boxed{125^\circ}$,

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a circle, and A, B, C, D are all on the circle; A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and D is located on the right small arc from A to C. The figure connects AB, AC, BC, and at D there is an angle formed by chords DA and DC, so what is required is ∠ADC. Then reason: It is known that AB=AC, △ABC is an isosceles triangle, and vertex angle ∠BAC=70°. Therefore base angles ∠ABC=∠ACB=(180°-70°)/2=55°. Because A, D, C, B are concyclic, and ∠ABC and ∠ADC are opposite angles of a cyclic quadrilateral, they are supplementary. Thus ∠ADC=180°-55°=125°.

raw_record.question_text: In $\triangle ABC$, $AB=AC$, $\angle BAC=70^\circ$, and $\odot O$ is the circumcircle of $\triangle ABC$. Point $D$ is on the minor arc $\overset{\frown}{AC}$. What is the degree measure of $\angle D$?

method.method_draft: First read the diagram as a circle through A, B, C, with D also on the circle on the small arc from A to C; the angle labeled at D is formed by chords DA and DC, so it is \(\angle ADC\). From the text, use \(AB=AC\) and \(\angle BAC=70^\circ\) to compute the base angles of isosceles triangle ABC: \(\angle ABC=\angle ACB=(180^\circ-70^\circ)/2=55^\circ\). Since A, B, C, D are concyclic and B and D are opposite vertices of cyclic quadrilateral A-D-C-B, opposite angles are supplementary, so \(\angle ADC=180^\circ-55^\circ=125^\circ\).

method.method_draft: Read from the diagram that \(\angle D\) is the inscribed angle \(\angle ADC\), with D on the minor arc AC, so this angle intercepts the major arc AC. From the text, compute \(\angle ABC=55^\circ\) because \(AB=AC\) and \(\angle A=70^\circ\). By the inscribed angle theorem, \(\angle ABC\) intercepts the minor arc AC, so the minor arc AC measures \(2\cdot55^\circ=110^\circ\). Therefore the major arc AC measures \(360^\circ-110^\circ=250^\circ\). Since \(\angle ADC\) intercepts that major arc, \(\angle ADC=250^\circ/2=125^\circ\).
